title: Alex Zanardi, former F1 driver and Paralympic champion, dies aged 59
content:
Former Formula 1 driver Alex Zanardi, who later became a Paralympic gold medallist, has died at the age of 59.

The Italian, who raced in Formula One from 1991 to 1994 and again in 1999, was involved in a motor racing accident in September 2001 at the Lausitzring track in Germany which resulted in both his legs being amputated.

“It is with deep sorrow ​that the family announces the passing of Alessandro Zanardi, which occurred suddenly yesterday ‌evening,  May 1,” read a statement from Zanardi’s family on Saturday.

“Alex died peacefully, surrounded by the affection of those closest to him.”

The Bologna-born driver represented Jordan, Minardi and Lotus in F1 but switched to race in the U.S. Cart championship, which he won in 1997 and 1998, before a brief return to F1.

After his 2001 injury, Zanardi took up para-cycling and won two gold medals at the 2012 Paralympics in London, in the individual H4 time trial and the individual H4 road race, followed by a silver medal in the mixed H1-4 team relay.

Four years later in Rio de Janeiro, he won a gold and a silver medal.

In 2020, Zanardi sustained serious head injuries after being struck by a truck during a charity paracycling relay in Tuscany, and would spend years undergoing treatment.

Stefano Domenicali, president and CEO of F1, released a statement in tribute of his “dear friend” Zanardi.

“He was truly an inspirational person, as a human and as an athlete. I will always carry with me his extraordinary strength,” Domenicali said. “He faced challenges that would have stopped anyone, yet he continued to look forward, always with a smile and a stubborn determination that inspired us all.

“While his loss is profoundly felt, his legacy remains strong.”

Italy’s prime minister Giorgia Meloni said the nation had lost “a great champion and an extraordinary man, who was capable of turning every challenge of life into a lesson in courage, strength, and dignity.”

Meloni added: “He gave all of us much more than a victory: he gave hope, pride, and the strength to never give up”

The International Automobile Federation (FIA), the governing body of motor sport, said in a tribute statement on Saturday that Zanardi was “one of sport’s most admired competitors and an enduring symbol of courage and determination.”

The Italian Olympic Committee (CONI) called for a minute of silence to be observed across Italian sporting events this weekend in honour of Zanardi.

“We’ve lost a great champion and a great man, who was capable of bouncing back multiple times when faced with life’s difficulties,” said CONI president Luciano Buonfiglio.

Clubs from across Italian soccer also joined in the tributes for Zanardi.

Milan posted that the former racer was an “extraordinary champion, man of great values and authentic example”, while their city rivals Inter said it “stands in solidarity with the family in this moment of grief.”

Bologna, the club of Zanardi’s home city, said: “You taught us that courage, strength of will, and passion can overcome every obstacle. Farewell Alex, and thank you. Your example will live on forever.”

Juventus, the 36-time champion of Italy, posted: “We join in the mourning for the passing of Alex Zanardi, an example of dedication, passion, and love for sport and for life.”
